title: Monthly Progress Report No. 7
key_sentences: Good progress was made on the steel frame in September, and the first-floor slab was poured on 24 September.
If the network operator confirms the new connection date, we expect to recover five of the ten days by the end of the year.
There were no reportable accidents during the month.
Brickwork to the north elevation started on 15 September.
Two brick panels were rebuilt after the sample panel was rejected for colour variation.
Ratings are shown as high, medium or low after the mitigation in place.
Both first-aid cases were minor cuts.
A toolbox talk on handling sheet materials was given to all trades on 18 September.

rows: Complete. As-built drainage survey issued on 29 September.
Complete, including roof steelwork over the hall.
Zone C slab moved to October to suit the steel erector’s second visit.
Started late because of the brick delivery; extra gang from 1 October.
Recovery plan agreed; ground floor classrooms first.
Substation connection later than the revised date of 9 November
Temporary supply from a generator for testing; weekly calls with the network operator
Scaffold sheeting on the north and east elevations; heated enclosure if needed
Long lead time for the hall’s folding partition
Order placed in September; design freeze agreed with the school
Asbestos found in the link corridor of the existing building
Refurbishment survey completed; licensed contractor on standby
Additional acoustic panels in the music room
Relocate the cycle shelter to the east boundary
Extra drainage gully at the staff car park

list_items.text: Complete the zone C floor slab.
Install decking and edge trims in the week of 5 October.
Pour the slab on 14 October, weather permitting.
Continue brickwork to the north and east elevations with two gangs.
Start first-fix mechanical and electrical work in the ground floor classrooms.

notes: Two-page construction progress report; body in Book Antiqua, headings and labels in Century Gothic. Letterhead line (contractor and project) repeats on both pages and is listed once; footer has the report reference and "1 / 2", "2 / 2". The reporting-period line under the title is body text. Table 1 "Key facts" is a captioned key/value table FLOATED to the right; the summary paragraphs wrap beside it (read the table where it starts, i.e. after the period line and before "1 Summary", or treat it as a sidebar). Table 2 has vertical rules between columns and a rule under the header but NO horizontal rules between rows; its comment cells are top-aligned and may wrap. Table 3 (risks) is a full grid with coloured rating cells. Section 4 shows four figure boxes side by side ("0 reportable accidents" etc.); they are body text, not a table. Section 5 is a list whose markers "1", "2", "3" and "1.1", "1.2" are generated by CSS counters, so items carry no marker (level 0 and level 1). Table 4 has a total row whose label spans two columns and whose last cell is empty (""). Section numbers in headings are typed.
